energy_oil.rationale: Facts: the Iran war premium unwound after the US midterms. Like-for-like Jan-27 Brent futures fell 13% from $113.43 (Oct 30) to $98.32 (Nov 6), front-month WTI fell from $104.12 to $90.83 and XLE fell 12%. Physical and supply signals are bearish: Aramco cut December Asian OSPs by $2 (Arab Light at its widest discount since June 2020), Dubai flipped into contango for the first time since July, JPMorgan puts the October surplus at 1.4 mb/d, the IEA sees a large 2027 surplus once Hormuz flows recover, and the Nov 29 full OPEC+ meeting on 2027 baselines risks a market-share contest. US activity is not being cut (604 rigs, +56 y/y; FANG/DVN/EOG/COP capex steady to higher). Offsets keep this from -2: renewed 'minor' US strikes on Qeshm (Nov 6), 11 ships attacked in the week, CENTCOM combat preparations, FGE's mid-Nov to mid-Dec limited-strike window, and US distillate stocks at their lowest since 2003. The upside gap risk is $10-20/bbl and two-sided.

materials_mining_metals.rationale: Facts: copper fell to a 17-week low (~$6.18-6.22/lb, about -5.5% m/m) on AI data-centre regulation fears after the midterms, and copper miners fell with it (FCX -7.5% and SCCO -6.5% on Nov 5; FCX about -11% from late October). Non-China rare-earth names lost their scarcity premium (MP -15% w/w) as the US-China truce looks set to roll forward (USTR proposal to Jan 9, 2027). Against that, physical supply is very tight (Shanghai spot copper premium at a record, SHFE stocks near a three-year low, smelter cuts), Grasberg stays constrained into 2027, copper is still about +26% y/y with FCX unit costs near $2/lb, gold majors keep returning large amounts of capital, and SA PGM output is shrinking (Sibanye SA PGM -10% y/y, US PGM guidance cut ~15% after a strike) while the 4E basket is +15% y/y. Interpretation: demand sentiment and supply tightness offset; neutral with a downside skew because copper miners now trade as an AI-capex proxy.

gold_precious.rationale: Facts: COMEX gold futures rebounded from a one-year low of $3,898.9 (Oct 30) to $4,113.5 (Nov 5) and $4,074.9 (Nov 6), about +4.5% on the week but still ~23% below the January peak; the bounce came from the midterm dollar and yield drop and lower oil. Strong October payrolls (+165k) pushed December Fed hike odds back to ~70-75%, gold was sold for margin in the Nov 5 equity rout, and Goldman cut its end-2026 forecast to $4,150 (end-2027 $4,800). Central-bank buying is a floor (WGC Q3 321t, +42% y/y; Goldman nowcast 85t/month). Miners' ~2.8x beta came from extremely oversold breadth, and spot sits $200-250 below Q3 realised prices while Q4 AISC guidance rises (Newmont ~$1,900). Platinum's rally conflicts with WPIC's 2026 surplus forecast. Interpretation: gold is trading as a Fed/real-rate asset, not a hedge; neutral. Barrick (Nov 9) and US CPI (Nov 10) are the next tests.

commodities_broad.rationale: Facts: energy, the largest weight in broad indices, lost much of its war premium (Jan-27 Brent -13% w/w, WTI -11% to -13%; the Bloomberg Commodity Spot Index fell 2.04% on Nov 4). Industrial metals are softer (copper -5% m/m to a 17-week low) and grains are heavy on supply (soybeans at an 11-week low on slower Chinese buying and a record US crop; wheat at a six-month low). The Fed is pricing a December hike (~75%). Gold is roughly flat-to-up and cannot offset energy. Offsets: tight oil products (US distillates at a 2003 low), record-tight Chinese physical copper and a live Middle East strike window make the risk two-sided. Interpretation: mild headwind for broad baskets over 1-3 months.

regime_notes: Two common factors drove commodities this week. First, the US midterm sweep unwound the Iran war premium: the White House blamed the war for the loss, Qatar-mediated talks advanced, and Brent fell ~13% on a like-for-like contract to ~$98, with Aramco OSP cuts and Dubai contango confirming a looser physical market. That move is reversible in one decision: minor US strikes resumed on Nov 6 and FGE sees a limited strike window from mid-November to mid-December. Second, the AI/data-centre selloff hit copper and copper miners (17-week low, FCX -7.5% on Nov 5), so materials now trade partly as an AI-capex proxy while Chinese physical copper stays record-tight. Gold behaves as a real-rate asset: it rose on the lower dollar and yields, then fell on strong payrolls and ~75% December hike odds, with central-bank buying as a floor. Data caveats: the $118 Brent figure is the Oct 30 expiring futures settle and $135 is the Oct 2 Dated spot print; continuous BZ=F overstates the week's drop by ~$4.2 because of the Dec-to-Jan roll; the Nov 10 rare-earth cliff looks defused by a truce roll-forward (USTR proposal to Jan 9, 2027) but MOFCOM has not confirmed.
